chunk_findings.detail: The set comprehension that builds `adopted` dereferences `e.data.get("adopted_from")` for *every* event in the log, with no guard. But `_gather`'s own loop a few lines below deliberately writes `d = ev.data or {}` before touching `.get(...)`, i.e. the code in this very file assumes `Event.data` can be falsy/None. The loop protects itself by testing `ev.kind not in _KINDS` *first*; the comprehension tests nothing. So any log that contains one event with `data is None` — precisely the non-session events the loop would have skipped — makes `_gather` raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`. Because both `list_sessions` and `show_session` call `_gather` first, both entry points die with an unhandled `AttributeError` instead of returning rows or raising `SessionViewError`. Repro: `list_sessions([Event(kind="other", data=None)], cfg)` (any fixture whose log carries a payload-less event). The fix is `(e.data or {}).get("adopted_from")` to match the loop's own convention.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/session_view.py:45 (`_gather`, the `adopted = {...}` comprehension)

chunk_findings.detail: The comprehension `{e.data["adopted_from"] for e in events if e.data.get("adopted_from")}` dereferences `e.data` unconditionally (`e.data.get(...)`), whereas the very next loop over the same events deliberately writes `d = ev.data or {}` — i.e. the module already treats `data` as possibly `None`/absent. For any log containing an event with `data is None` (the canonical case being a `session.ended` event written without a payload, since only `session.started` is documented to carry `model`/`tool`/`summary`), `SessionView._gather` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` before it ever reaches the guarded loop, so both `session list` and `session show` blow up on that log instead of listing/showing. The guarded comprehension would be `(e.data or {}).get("adopted_from")`, or the set should be built inside the loop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/session_view.py:_gather (the `adopted = {...}` comprehension)

chunk_findings.detail: `show_session` redacts `model`, `tool`, `summary` and every entry's `text`, and the module docstring promises "Every free-text field goes through the same redaction the export documents use." But the item labels are emitted raw: the top-level `items=_items(s)` list and each entry's `"item": e["item"]`. `_gather` stores `"item": d.get("item", "")` straight from the log, so if an item label is free text (e.g. an item titled with a URL or a path containing a token — the kind of string `redact_text` exists to mask), `ddflow session show <id>` prints it verbatim while the prompt/note text next to it is redacted. Since `_items` feeds `export` documents too, this diverges from "the same redaction the export documents use". The item value needs `redact_text(e["item"], cfg).text` (and the returned list built from redacted labels).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/session_view.py:show_session

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s entire purpose — and an explicit acceptance criterion — is to prove `session show` works when `export sessions` is off, but the test never turns that setting off. `_fixture` only calls `ddflow init` and appends raw log events; nothing in this test (or its helpers) writes a config that sets `export.sessions=false` or removes any export artifact. Consequently the test runs under whatever the ambient/default configuration happens to be. Concretely: if a later change flips the default to enabled, or if a prior test in the session enables exports, this test still passes and no longer verifies the disabled case; a regression where `show` requires `export.sessions=true` would not be caught by the one test named for that condition. The test must explicitly put the repo into the disabled state (e.g. via `run_cli(repo, "config", "set", "export.sessions", "false")` or an equivalent fixture) before asserting `show` succeeds.
